design.summary: Decision D33 (team use) is written into rewrite/spec/ and all four checks are clean. One hub topic (team-use) explains it end to end and links four owning topics, three commands (sync, claim take, claim release), two records (work-claim, clone), the [team] section, five tables (claim scopes, three check tables with 26 checks, the keys) and the two-clone proof. 65 existing files got a short passage under a heading that says "decision D33; built when the build widens"; nothing was added to a table the slice uses. Five packages, M1 to M5, are registered and placed after the flag packages and before the proofs; none is on the slice. The ledger has 24 entries (D33-1 to D33-24), each in its package's list; three are for slice units to build now (D33-9 record schemas stay open, D33-13 no remote named in the worktree library, D33-21 no machine paths in tracked text) and none changes what the slice does. I also re-triaged the earlier finding P3OPS-13 to M1 and M2, because its proposed lease contradicts the claim. Every git fact stated was run on a scratch bare repository with two clones (git 2.50.1) or read in the git manual. Four questions need the user.

M2: Claims. The work-claim record and schema, the four scopes, taking in survey, admission and feature route, releasing at the checkpoint, vsdd claim take and claim release, withholding at sync, claiming what is in flight when team use turns on. Depends on M1, S3, S4, G5, G4b, C1, C2, H6, B4a

M3: Who, decisions across clones, and hand-off. Person and clone in the records and on every state commit, a settlement published at once and the rule for two settlements, order by stored link, the red record carried in the closure, story branches pushed at the checkpoint, ids minted inside a sync. Depends on M1, M2, S4, S6, G2, G3, H7, K1

M4: Team delivery, hand commits and a wave on a team. Pull requests only, hand commits noticed, listed, made review items and never rewritten, a wave whose stories several clones hold. Depends on M2, M3, G2, G3, G4a, G4b, G6a, G6b, G7, A6a, B5, W2, W3, W7

Order of work: after the flag packages and before the proofs, M1, M2, M3, M4, M5; none is on the thin slice; build-plan.md now counts 85 packages
checks: T-JOIN: a refusal of vsdd init. Refuses to mount state another clone wrote while team.enabled is not true; answers solo and prints the two ways on (turn team use on at the first clone, or a person runs init --only-clone)

T-SOLO: a refusal of the state push while team use is off. Refuses to combine and push when the remote state branch holds commits this clone lacks; names their authors and the line that turns team use on

T-REMOTE: a step of every fetch and push. Refuses a branch with no upstream when the clone has several remotes or none; never reads a remote's name from code or factory.toml; a push the remote's own rule declines is reported and not retried

T-FRESH: the opening sync of every survey, before any precondition. Refuses a run that needs a claim this clone does not hold when the remote is unreachable, state is diverged or blocked, or the sync refused; a run on claims already held starts marked refreshed: false

T-VERSION: a step of the sync and a precondition of the survey. Refuses a factory.toml with an unknown schema (built), and a run or push from a plugin below team.min_plugin; every state commit carries Plugin: and Clone:

T-COMBINE: a step of the sync. Decides each path once: a code-written record changed on both sides keeps the remote's and sets this clone's aside, named; text changed on both sides gets git's three-way merge, and a conflict or a result that fails its check is diverged with nothing changed

T-INCOMING: a step of the sync on every arriving commit. Refuses to build on a record that fails its schema or cap (its unit stops, commit and author named); lists commits that changed a record outside the factory
T-LOCAL: a step of the flush and the sync. Refuses to commit or push any path under .factory/local/, and to push a factory.toml whose path or glob keys hold an absolute or home-relative path

T-WHO: a refusal of the flush and of every claim, and fields the tool writes. Refuses to commit state, claim or publish a settlement with no user.name or user.email; writes person and clone into claim, decision, delivery and commit trailers; compares them with nothing

T-ORDER: a rule of the stores, held by a test per ordering function and the proof's clock scenario. Refuses to order two tracked records by their times; latest and newer are read from a stored follows link

T-CLAIM: a refusal of survey, the admission commands, feature route, story deliver and the stores' write path. Refuses a run on a scope another clone holds (names holder and the three ways on), a delivery of a story not held, and a tracked write to a unit not held

T-PUBLISH: the one way a claim is taken or changed. Refuses to hold a claim the remote has not accepted: one commit on the remote's head adding only claim files, pushed as a fast-forward; the loser of two pushes fetches and has lost; five attempts, then busy

T-RELEASE: a step of the checkpoint, and vsdd claim release. Removes run claims at every checkpoint and the claims of stories delivered, descoped or never begun; refuses to release a claim another clone holds or one with a live run
T-TAKEOVER: vsdd claim take, person only in a terminal. Refuses any call from a tool call, session or unattended run, and a claim that changed since it was shown; no claim expires; records taken_from

T-HOLD: a step of the sync after the combine. Refuses to publish a change to anything a scope covers while another clone holds that scope: the remote's stands, this clone's is set aside and named, its run on the unit ends

T-SWITCH: a step of the first sync that sees team.enabled on the clone that set it. Refuses to turn on with state.push false, delivery.mode not pr, or no remote; then claims every story in flight on that clone

T-HANDOFF: a step of the checkpoint and of claim release. Refuses to leave a story's work only on one clone: copies the red record into the closure and pushes the story branch as a fast-forward; a release is refused if that fails
T-MINT: a rule of commands that mint an id more than one claim could mint (epic, story of E-0, change request, idea, spike, review report). Refuses to return an id the remote has not accepted

T-SETTLE: a step of the sync, of vsdd decide and of the decisions rule. Refuses a second settlement of a decision the remote holds settled: the first pushed stands, the second is set aside and its person is told who settled it and both choices

T-DELIVERY: a refusal of vsdd story deliver. Refuses local delivery on a team; records merged_by; adopts a pull request merged outside the tool only when the merged change has the reviewed patch id, else counts its merge as a hand commit

T-NOTICE: a report in the survey, binding in the wave and release gates. Lists first-parent commits on the target branch that no delivery or release recorded; fails with history_rewritten when the range cannot be measured; never changes a baseline

T-BRANCH: a step of the survey and of delivery for each story held. Refuses to drop commits that reached the remote story branch from elsewhere: records them, merges them in under their own ids, and returns conflict when they do not merge
T-ITEMS: items of the verdict. Refuses a converged verdict, and so a delivery, a closed wave or a release decision, while an item hand:<12 hex> is not marked checked

T-GAP: a blocked result of kind spec_gap from the reviewer of a hand commit. Refuses to close the perimeter as if the specification still described the code: opens spec-gap, and the release packet lists every hand commit

T-NEVER: a rule of the delivery and worktree libraries, held by tests on real repositories. Refuses to rebase, amend, squash away, revert or force-push over a person's commit; a branch with one is updated by merging the target in

T-WAVE: a step of the wave survey and a refusal of vsdd gate wave. Refuses to measure the wave while a story held by another clone is undelivered (pending, never moved); the run returns partial and names holders
design_choices: The claim: four scopes (a story, held until delivered, released or taken over; a cycle's run slot, which covers a wave and a release; the specification set; the opening of a cycle, the last three held for one run or act). A claim is a file on the state branch made by a push the remote accepts from one clone only; everyone sees it after a fetch. No expiry, because git has no liveness: a person takes a gone clone's claim over in a terminal, and the old holder is told at its next sync

Freshness: every survey syncs before reading preconditions and every checkpoint syncs in place of its push. Unreachable (offline or no credentials, one case, never a prompt or an unbounded wait): a clone may continue claims it holds, marked not refreshed, and is refused new claims. The briefing never fetches

The state branch under several writers: one file per record and one holder per unit; pushes combine by a merge commit built without touching the mount, which is then fast-forwarded. Records changed on both sides keep the remote's and set the other aside, named; text gets git's three-way merge or ends diverged for a person. A hand-edited record is checked for shape; whether it is true is stated as unmeasured

Shared and local: tracked state is shared; runs, steps, evidence, lock, markers and jobs stay on the machine. A unit moves, a run does not. Hand-off continues from the last checkpoint, which also pushes story branches; nothing is pushed more often. Gate results are measured again, except the red record, which travels in the closure; closed units are trusted

Who: the person from the clone's git configuration plus a clone id, in the claim, the decision record, the delivery and every state commit's author and trailers. No authority is checked and no key names a person or role

Decisions: seen after a sync, settled by any person on any clone, published at once (terminal: before and after; typed: by a detached sync, else the next survey). Of two settlements the first pushed stands and the second person is told

Delivery on a team: pull requests and CI only (pr mode, unchanged); local delivery is for one clone or no remote. A moving integration branch is handled by the recorded base, the patch-bound verdict and the existing conflict repair

Hand commits: on the integration branch, any first-parent commit no delivery or release recorded; on a story branch, any commit that reached the remote from another clone. Listed, never changing a baseline, made review items, sent to the test-writer when they touch a frozen test and to spec-gap when the specification is behind; never rebased, reverted or forced over

Waves on a team: stories of one wave can be held by different people; one clone at a time drives the wave through the cycle claim; the gate is run by whoever holds that claim once every story is delivered, descoped or moved

Versions and settings: the schema number refuses an unknown state format; team.min_plugin refuses an old plugin; every state commit says which version wrote it. All of factory.toml is shared; the remote's name, identity, credentials and .factory/local/ belong to one clone
Remotes: the remote is the branch's upstream, whatever it is called; only ordinary branches are used; credentials are never assumed; no time from one clone is compared with another's

Solo use: team.enabled defaults to false, and with it off or with no remote nothing runs or waits. The one difference: a second clone cannot mount the state until team use is on or a person says the first clone is gone, and a push that finds the remote moved stops instead of combining

The proof: sixteen scenarios on two clones of one bare repository (remotes named shared and upstream, two identities, one clock three hours behind), each with an end condition, plus one headless story-tier run with two sessions

The thin slice: 24 ledger entries; three for units to build now (keep tracked record schemas open; read the remote from the branch's upstream in the worktree library; no machine paths in tracked text), none changing what the slice does on one machine
open_questions: Solo use and a second clone: team.enabled defaults to off, so a person who works alone and re-clones (a new laptop) must run vsdd init --only-clone once, and one who alternates two machines must turn team use on. That is one extra person-only step in a rare flow, against the clause that solo use has no extra step. Accept it, or should team behaviour be on whenever a remote exists (a fetch and a claim push on every run for everyone)?

Decision D4 was answered once per project. On a team that answer (which tool calls the plugin approves by itself) then applies on machines whose person was never asked; setup only shows it to a person who joins. Should each joining person be asked for their own machine?

Team delivery is pull requests only, and pr mode is specified through one vendor's command-line tool. The design now asks G4a to put the host operations behind one module (ledger D33-18). Is a team on another Git host in scope for 1.0, so that a second implementation is built?
Does cutover wait for the two-clone proof (M5)? As written it does not: cutover waits for E3 and E4 only, and team use is simply not offered or documented as supported until M5 passes.

reviews.verdict:
The overall shape holds up, but it is not ready to build as written: no blockers, 11 major and 13 minor findings. Taking a claim by one push that the remote accepts from only one clone is sound: in 40 simultaneous rounds exactly one push won each time. The design is also right to give claims no expiry, to order nothing by clock, to hand off from what was pushed, and to list and review commits made by hand. The majors come from git behaving differently from what the design assumes, each reproduced in scratch repositories:
(1) The loser of a real push race gets "[remote rejected] (failed to update ref)", never "fetch first" (40 of 40 rounds), so the rule that retries only on "fetch first" reports every lost race as a remote's rule and never retries.
(2) A push the client gives up on (time limit, dropped connection) can still have landed on the remote, which leaves claims nobody knows they hold and duplicate minted ids.
(3) A rewound, force-pushed or deleted state branch is not detected: fetch accepts the forced update silently, the combine quietly restores what was dropped, and push recreates a deleted branch.
(4) A bare --force-with-lease after any fetch overwrote a teammate's commit.
(5) T-BRANCH reads the holder's own rebased commits as hand commits.
(6) The text says the story branch is pushed "to its upstream", and a branch made with --track from the target has the integration branch as its upstream, so a checkpoint can fast-forward main and skip the pull request.
(7) After a claim is accepted, the mount cannot fast-forward to it when it holds unpushed commits.
(8) A settlement can be acted on before any sync confirms it when the clone is offline.
(9) The sync is said to hold flush.lock across network calls; the built settle_decision and record writes give up after 3 s, so a decision typed during a sync fails.
(11) Forks and mirrors are not addressed: claims through two copies of one repository both succeed and nothing notices.
(12) On a team, the release still pushes the hotfix merge-back straight to the integration branch, which a protected repository refuses.
Separately, the ssh prompt test showed GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 does not stop ssh from prompting in a terminal, and the time limit leaves the ssh process running. No finding touches the thin slice path.

integrate.summary:
All 56 review findings are decided and the D33 design is corrected; none is rejected outright, left for a builder or put to the user. The four checks are clean.

The corrections that change the design most:

- **Git's answers are measured, not read.** Two new checks: T-PUSH judges every push by a fetch and a comparison of commits (lost race, declined, or accepted with the answer lost), and T-HISTORY stops the sync when the state branch was rewound or deleted.
- **No run without a fetch.** A survey starts a run only after a sync that ended `synced`; the offline allowance is gone. A settlement counts only once the remote holds it.
- **Story branches cannot land on the shared branch.** The tool takes only the remote from an upstream, pushes every branch under its own name, and the one forced push names the head it expects.
- **Hand commits are handled with team use off as well**, wherever the branch has an upstream.
- **Solo projects keep their behaviour.** A second clone mounts with a notice instead of being refused; `--only-clone` is removed.
- **The combine no longer uses `git merge-tree`.** It decides each path itself and merges text one file at a time, which also lowers the git floor to 2.34.
- **The sync holds `flush.lock` for local steps only**, never across the network.

I ran the git facts in scratch repositories on git 2.50.1 (macOS) and git 2.34.1 (Linux container); the ssh and askpass behaviour was run on Linux only, against a throwaway sshd. They are now `rewrite/spec/topics/team-git-facts.md`.

Structural changes: a sixth package M6 (settings, clone record, joining, preflight) is built first so M1 is the sync alone; a new table `sync-checks`; the two claim tables are renamed `work-claim-checks` and `work-claim-scopes`; `vsdd claim release` moves to M3. Six ledger entries were added (D33-25 to D33-30) and most of the existing 24 rewritten.

Two things touch the thin slice's units, neither changing what the slice does. D33-25 asks S3's `create_story` test to assert the new branch has no upstream. D33-13 now has `target_head` fetch the branch by its own name in pr mode, which the slice does not run.

Several choices tighten what a team may do and are listed under decisions_made: no offline runs, CI required for team use, team use refused in a hub, fork-only workflows unsupported, and a state branch that cannot require signatures or pull requests.
decisions_made: No run starts unless the survey's opening sync ended `synced`; there is no offline continuation, because clause 4c says a run starts from what the team has pushed.
A settlement counts only once the remote holds it: it is listed as unpublished from the moment it is written and reads as open to every gate, survey, route and delivery until then.
Every push of the state branch is judged by a fetch and a comparison of commits (T-PUSH), never by git's reason text or by the push failing.
A state branch that was rewound or deleted stops the sync (`rewritten`, `missing`); no sync recreates the branch or brings vanished commits back.
The tool takes only the remote from an upstream; every fetch and push names the branch's own ref in full, and an upstream that names another ref is refused.
A story branch is created at a commit id (no upstream) and pushed under its own name to the remote of its target branch.

The one push the tool forces names the head it expects (`--force-with-lease=<ref>:<delivery.pushed>`); rebasing a branch with no hand commit is kept, so the delivery design's patch-id rules are untouched.
Hand-commit handling keys on the branch having an upstream, not on `team.enabled`; a solo project with a remote gets its hand commits reviewed, and a project with no remote gets none of it.
With team use off a second clone mounts with a notice (decision D1 kept); `--only-clone` is removed; T-SOLO stops the first push that finds a second writer.
A clone already mounted when a team is formed joins by itself at its next push.
The combine is built path by path with `git merge-file` for text; `git merge-tree` is not used, so the git floor is 2.34 rather than 2.38.
Records are never merged, only chosen whole; `notes.json` alone is a union cut to its cap.
`flush.lock` is held for the sync's local steps only; `local/sync.lock` serialises whole syncs of one clone.
A sync is full at a survey, a checkpoint, `status --fix` or `vsdd sync` when no other run is live; every other sync is partial and commits only the paths its caller names.
A claim's removal is committed only together with the changes its scope covers; `open` is removed in the commit that adds the cycle record.
A full sync removes a run claim with no live run, and a story claim under which nothing was begun, without a person asking.
T-HOLD ends no run and releases no lock; a run that lost a unit is stopped at its next write and ends at its own checkpoint.
A wave run claims only the stories it can start (`limits.stories_per_wave_run`); the cycle-level runs of one cycle stay serialised by the `cycle` claim.
Team use requires `delivery.ci = "required"` as well as `pr` mode, per clause 4f.
Team use cannot be turned on in a multi-repository hub until that combination is designed and proved.
State commits stay unsigned (decision D2); a state branch that requires signatures or pull requests is not supported.
Every clone must push state and story branches to the one shared repository; a fork-only workflow is not supported, and `vsdd init --remote` chooses when several remotes hold the state.
No configuration key names the delivery's host module; the tool asks it whether it can serve the remote.
In `pr` mode `vsdd release` moves shared branches only through pull requests.
A pull request the host will merge later is the delivery state `queued`, which opens no decision.
The red record travels as its own tracked record under `cycles/<cycle>/red/`, with the evidence record's cap, not inside the closure.
The identity recorded is the one git itself would stamp (`git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` with `user.useConfigOnly`).
A clone has a label (host name by default, replaceable) that is shown in claims and decides nothing.
Network calls run with stdin from `/dev/null` in their own session, askpass disabled, and the whole process group killed at the time limit.
Time limits: 30 s per network call, 60 s for a sync inside a foreground command, 30 s for the claim; `vsdd sync` as a job for a clone far behind.
A sixth package M6 (settings, clone record, joining, preflight) is built before M1; `vsdd claim release` moves to M3; the delivery refusal moves to M4.
The setup passage that offers team use is delivered by M5 only once the proof passes.
The two claim tables are renamed `work-claim-checks` and `work-claim-scopes`; the commands `vsdd claim take` and `vsdd claim release` and the check T-CLAIM keep their names.
`follows` is stored only by decisions whose id carries no subject; open cycles are ordered by kind and id.
D33-13 (on the slice path) is amended so `target_head` fetches the branch by its own name and refuses a differing upstream ref; this is the pr-mode branch, which the slice does not run.

I wrote my two output files afterwards and did not run the build again; both parse as JSON. I tested the git commands the design rests on in scratch repositories, in the scratchpad and in an Ubuntu 22.04 container (git 2.34.1), on git 2.50.1 (macOS) and 2.34.1 (Linux). These hold: facts 1 to 4, 7, 8 (macOS only), 9, 11, 12 and 13. They cover race reasons, one winner, a lost answer measured by containment, upstreams with --track and at a commit id, push -u, ff-only refusing an equal file, ls-remote exit 2/128, git var identity, the explicit lease against the bare one, and the rev-list of arrived commits. The tests also found three things wrong. Fetching refs/heads/<b>:refs/heads/<b> into a checked-out branch exits 128. A non-forced fetch after a rewind exits 1. git diff --name-status reports a claim release plus take as R080 (see D33R-C-1 and C-2).

still_open.problem: The wave claim is capped by limits.stories_per_wave_run alone (default 24) and is said to be 'the ones runStories() can start', but runStories() also caps a batch by the agent budget, floor((agents_per_run - RUN.agents - CLOSE_RESERVE)/agents_per_story). With agents_per_run lowered, a wave run claims up to 24 stories but starts only a few, and the rest are blocked from teammates for the whole run.
still_open.proposed_fix: Claim the batch runStories() will start: the free units within min(stories_per_wave_run, the agent fit), computed by one function that the survey and the prelude both read. Correct the story scope's `when` and T-WAVE.

still_open.problem: The parallel-work table restates the no-claim rule ('spike, discover and a report-only maintain, at any time | They take no claim') outside work-claim-scopes.toml and omits its exception: opening a cycle takes `open`, the discover assess checkpoint included.
still_open.proposed_fix: Have the row say they take no claim for their run, and link [[table:work-claim-scopes]] for the rule and its exception.

still_open.problem: 'No claim expires', whose home is now T-TAKEOVER, is still restated in topics/team-claims.md, records/work-claim.md ('carries no expiry and no sign of life') and topics/team-use.md ('no program decides that a holder is gone').
still_open.proposed_fix: Keep the rule in T-TAKEOVER. The topics give the reason and link to it, and the record says only that `at` decides nothing.

still_open.problem: (a) T-PUBLISH's unmeasured cell says T-RELEASE removes an accepted lost-answer claim, but T-RELEASE removes only held=run claims and unbegun story claims. An `open`/`open.hotfix` claim (held=act) whose answer was lost, or whose command died before its push, stays held and refuses every other clone's opening of a cycle. (b) The sync that settles an `unknown` commit reports nothing (sync.md has no output field for it), so a person who re-runs a refused T-MINT command after that sync mints a duplicate.
still_open.proposed_fix: A full sync also removes an act-held claim of this clone when no command of this clone is running under it and its cycle record is absent. The sync result lists each unknown commit it settled, with what it carried (claim scope, minted path) and whether the remote had taken it.

still_open.problem: T-REMOTE says every fetch names refs/heads/<branch> on both sides. Tested on 2.34.1 and 2.50.1: a fetch into the checked-out state branch exits 128, so every sync would be `unreachable`. A fetch into a target branch that is not checked out moves the person's local branch. A non-forced fetch into the remote-tracking ref exits 1 after a rewind, so T-HISTORY's `rewritten` reads as `unreachable`. Fact 9's 'exit 0, forced update' holds only for a + refspec, and sync.md says the sync writes the remote-tracking ref. Ledger D33-13 (on the slice path, S3's target_head) carries the same wording.
still_open.proposed_fix: A push names refs/heads/<b> on both sides. A fetch is `git fetch <remote> +refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<b>`, never into refs/heads. Fact 9 says the + is what makes a rewind a forced update with exit 0. Amend D33-13 the same way before S3 builds, and add a pr-mode test that the local integration branch did not move, plus an M1 test that a rewound branch gives `rewritten`.

still_open.problem: Fact 6 names `git diff --name-status` as what the sync reads to decide each path. Porcelain diff detects renames by default. Tested on 2.34.1 and 2.50.1: releasing claims/story.S-1.json and taking claims/story.S-2.json in one commit is listed as one line, R080 S-1 -> S-2. A path-by-path combine then misses a removal and an addition.
still_open.proposed_fix: In T-COMBINE and fact 6, read both diffs with rename detection off (`git diff-tree -r --no-renames --name-status`), and test the release-plus-take commit.

still_open.problem: T-PUSH's lost-race test ('the head is no longer the commit the push was built on') also matches a rewound state branch. T-PUBLISH and T-MINT then build again on the rewound head and take the accepted commit into the mount through T-COMBINE, which brings the vanished commits back. The arrivals between the two heads skip T-INCOMING and T-HOLD. clone.md updates sync.remote_head at any successful fetch, so T-PUSH's own fetch can make the next T-HISTORY pass, and the rewind is undone silently.
still_open.proposed_fix: A lost race requires that the new head contains the push's base; otherwise every caller answers `rewritten`. After a lost race, T-PUBLISH and T-MINT run T-HISTORY, T-INCOMING and T-HOLD before building again. Write sync.remote_head only after T-HISTORY accepts a fetched head. Add a rewind between the opening sync and the claim push to scenario 7.

still_open.problem: T-RELEASE's full-sync removal of 'a story claim under which nothing was begun and no run is live' (and of run-held claims with no live run) matches a claim just taken with `vsdd claim take`, which starts no run. It is removed by the opening sync of the very survey that claim-take.md says 'enters the claim as its own'. taken_from is lost and the story is briefly free to any clone. Whether 'begun' is read from the local branch or the remote one is not said.
still_open.proposed_fix: Measure 'begun' on the remote story branch as well as locally. Do not auto-remove a claim carrying taken_from until a run of this clone has entered it or a person releases it. Add the case to scenario 28.

still_open.problem: `vsdd sync` is a job keyed by command and branch with no commit. The decisions rule starts it detached and nothing collects the result. The built job layer (jobs.py _serves) serves an uncollected finished result to the next call with the same key, so a later `vsdd sync` returns the hook's old outcome and runs no sync.
still_open.proposed_fix: Start the rule's sync under its own key (for example subject settle:<decision id>), or make `vsdd sync` attach only to a running job. State this in long-commands' Team use passage and test it.

still_open.problem: When T-SOLO joins a clone that was mounted with team use off to a team formed meanwhile, nothing claims that clone's in-flight stories (T-SWITCH does this only on the switching clone). T-HANDOFF pushes branches only of claimed stories, so another clone can take the story as free and restart it from base, which is double work (4b). Scenario 17 gives B no story in flight.
still_open.proposed_fix: T-SOLO's join claims, as T-SWITCH does, every undelivered story with commits beyond its base that no other clone claims, and reports the others for a person. Extend scenario 17.

still_open.problem: The head rule names 'three exceptions' to team-only checks, but T-DELIVERY (and D33-17) runs all but its two team refusals in every pr-mode delivery with team use off: the host-module refusal, `queued`, adoption, merged_by. config/team.md 'Off' and team-use.md 'One clone' omit it. config/team.md says 'No survey fetches', though pr mode fetches the target branch. merged_by is to name a clone that has no record when team use is off.
still_open.proposed_fix: Name T-DELIVERY (less its two team refusals) as an exception in the head rule, config/team.md and team-use.md. Say merged_by holds no clone when team use is off. Reword to 'no survey fetches the state branch'.

still_open.problem: A second sync waits on local/sync.lock with no limit. A `vsdd sync` job has ten minutes per network call, so a survey, checkpoint or decide queued behind it passes the 60-second foreground budget that T-FRESH relies on to stay inside the Bash default.
still_open.proposed_fix: Count the wait for sync.lock against the caller's 60-second budget and answer `busy` at its end, changing nothing. Add a case with a slow sync job holding the lock while a survey starts.

still_open.problem: Story-branch pushes are judged by exit status, since T-PUSH covers only the state branch. If the forced push after a rebase is accepted but its answer is lost, and T-NEVER's 'put the branch back' runs, T-BRANCH finds the rebased copies reachable from neither head. It records the holder's own commits as hand commits and merges them in: the doubled history S-5 named. The git cherry filter that S-5 proposed was dropped without a reason.
still_open.proposed_fix: Judge every story-branch push as T-PUSH judges a state push (fetch, compare, set delivery.pushed when accepted). In T-BRANCH, also drop arrived commits whose patch id is already on the local branch (git cherry). Add a case with a post-receive hook that outlasts the client's limit.
